notes:
Summary: Evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity SLA - Marigold runs low-latency reranking at scale for ad auction stack. Primary ask: guaranteed sustained throughput (min tokens/sec) across reserved GPU pool with well-defined concurrency caps and burst policy. Key business driver = predictable tail latency during peak auctions and cost predictability for seasonality.

Recent activity:
- 2026-01-20 discovery call (Alyssa + Diego): high-level requirements, introduced Dedicated and Private options. customer: wants on-prem-like controls for partner data.
- 2026-02-12 technical deep-dive (ff_20260212_1723_callID): tokenization and request fanout explained. Marigold provided real traffic histogram (QPS, payload sizes) — peak windows ~ 2x daily spikes.
- 2026-02-25 bench kickoff: SE to run workload replay against a 16xA100-equivalent reserved pool.
- 2026-03-03 design review (ff_20260303_0910_design_review): proposed routing policy, KV prefix caching, and fallback to quantized models for overload.
- 2026-03-04 contract & SLA workshop with procurement + legal (Alyssa, legal reps): legal pushed back on uptime SLA language and penalty caps.

Technical requirements (customer-specified):
- Sustained throughput target: minimum 220,000 tokens/sec across the reserved fleet during peak windows (30m rolling), based on replayed production mix.
- Concurrency cap: prefer soft per-customer concurrency cap of 6,000 concurrent requests (avg request size ~ 45 tokens) leading to protection against noisy tenants.
- Burst policy: allow up to 2.5x sustained throughput for 10 minutes (burst window) with guaranteed admission for priority routes (auction-critical). Bursts beyond that should trigger graceful degradation -> fallback quantized model or queueing.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 220ms and p99 < 480ms for 64-token responses when running on dedicated pool under sustained target; target tighter for priority routes p95 < 150ms.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial commit = 16xA100-equivalent GPUs (customer expects growth to 32 within 6 months). Need a mapping from tokens/sec target to GPU count under our kernel/quantization profiles.
- Routing/fallback: must support model variant routing (float32 -> int8 quantized) automatically with no API change; automatic retry/failover to adjacent region or lower-tier pool.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms and KV cache hit rates required for QBRs.

Negotiation points / open items:
- Minimum guaranteed tokens/sec number: Marigold insists on contractual min = 220k tps sustained; Redwood proposed 200k as baseline with performance review at month 1. Customer pushing for 220k + credits if not met.
- Burst definition: customer wants unlimited bursts up to 3x for highest-priority routes; Redwood counters with 2.5x for 10m then throttling. Need SRE input and cost model.
- Concurrency enforcement: customer wants token-based throttles rather than request-based caps. Engineering to confirm whether we can enforce token caps at admission time.
- SLA penalties & credits: legal disagreement on credit formula. Marigold wants linear credits starting at 99.5% uptime; Redwood standard is 99.7% for Dedicated.
- Maintenance windows: Marigold requests <1 scheduled maintenance/month for dedicated pool; Redwood engineering suggests monthly maintenance with configurable blackout windows.

POC / next steps:
- SE run: 24h continuous replay test (Diego) using Marigold production traces to validate GPU mapping and show p95/p99 under sustained 220k tokens/sec. Target date: 2026-03-10.
- Deliver throughput-to-GPU sizing doc (by Redwood) and cost delta for 220k vs 200k baseline.
- Legal to exchange SLA markups — Alyssa to re-send redline package by 2026-03-08.
- Procurement: informal cost approval expected by Mar 20; formal PO after SLA sign-off.

Quotes / paraphrases from calls:
- "We need predictability — if the pool drops tokens during an auction window we lose revenue." — Head of Product
- "Bursting is non-negotiable for Black Friday-like events; we need guaranteed headroom or defined credits." — Ops lead

Staging notes: include drive links to replay artifacts and current draft SLA. -> see linked_drive_docs. POC metrics will be uploaded to shared folder.

Sales tactics suggested: propose a tiered commitment: 200k baseline guaranteed + optional +20% burst add-on for fixed monthly premium. Offer a 60-day performance review clause that allows scale adjustments. Highlight Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + KV cache) to lower effective GPU count.
